_meta.note: 30 high-quality Part 2 cue cards across the seven canonical IELTS Speaking categories: person, place, object, experience, event, activity, media. Each card has 4 prompt bullets and 3 Part 3 follow-up questions for the same theme.

cards.prompt: Describe a person who has had a significant influence on your life.
bullets: How long you have known them
What they did that influenced you
And explain why their influence has been significant
part3Questions: What qualities make a person genuinely influential?
How does the influence of family compare with that of friends?
Do you think social media influencers have a positive or negative impact on young people?

cards.prompt: Describe a teacher you remember from your school years.
bullets: What was special about their teaching style
And explain why you still remember them
part3Questions: What makes a teacher truly memorable?
How has the role of teachers changed in the last twenty years?
Should teachers be paid more, and why?

cards.prompt: Describe an older person you admire.
bullets: What they have done in their life
And explain why you admire them
part3Questions: What can younger generations learn from older people?
Do you think older people are respected enough in your country?
How can communities support older people who live alone?

cards.prompt: Describe a friend who you would like to spend more time with.
bullets: And explain why you would like to spend more time with them
part3Questions: What makes a friendship last for many years?
Are friendships made online as strong as those made face-to-face?
How do friendships change as people get older?

cards.prompt: Describe a place in your hometown that you find interesting.
bullets: What you can do or see there
And explain why you find it interesting
part3Questions: Why do some places attract more tourists than others?
How important is it to preserve historical places in a city?
Should governments invest more in public spaces such as parks and squares?

cards.prompt: Describe a city you would like to visit in the future.
bullets: And explain why you want to visit it
part3Questions: What factors usually influence people's choice of holiday destination?
How does international tourism affect local communities?
Is it better to travel abroad or to explore your own country?

cards.prompt: Describe a quiet place where you like to spend time alone.
bullets: And explain why you find it relaxing
part3Questions: Why do people sometimes need time alone?
Are quiet public places more difficult to find than they used to be?
How does the place where someone lives affect their wellbeing?

cards.prompt: Describe a building you find architecturally impressive.
bullets: And explain why you find it impressive
part3Questions: What factors should architects consider when designing public buildings?
How important is it to preserve old buildings rather than demolish them?
Do modern buildings have less character than older ones?

cards.prompt: Describe a piece of technology you use every day.
bullets: What this piece of technology is
How long you have had it
And explain how your life would be different without it
part3Questions: How has everyday technology changed how people communicate?
Are people becoming too dependent on technology?
Should there be limits on how much technology children can use?

cards.prompt: Describe a gift you received that means a lot to you.
bullets: Who gave it to you and when
Why they gave it to you
And explain why it is meaningful
part3Questions: Is it more important for a gift to be expensive or thoughtful?
Why do people in different cultures give gifts on different occasions?
Do you think giving experiences is better than giving physical gifts?

cards.prompt: Describe an item of clothing you wear often.
bullets: And explain why you like it
part3Questions: How important is fashion in your culture?
Do you think people are too influenced by fashion trends?
What are the environmental costs of fast fashion?

cards.prompt: Describe a book that has had an impact on you.
bullets: And explain how it affected you
part3Questions: Why do some people read more than others?
How does reading fiction differ from reading non-fiction in terms of benefits?
Will printed books still exist in fifty years?

cards.prompt: Describe a time when you helped someone.
bullets: And explain how you felt afterwards
part3Questions: Why do some people volunteer their time to help others?
Should schools require students to do community service?
Is it the responsibility of governments or individuals to help those in need?

cards.prompt: Describe a difficult decision you had to make.
bullets: When you had to make it
And explain how you reached a decision
part3Questions: What makes some decisions harder than others?
Should young people make their own decisions about their education?
Is it better to make decisions quickly or to take time to think them through?

cards.prompt: Describe a time when you learned something new.
bullets: How long it took to learn
And explain why this was important to you
part3Questions: What is the best way to learn a new skill as an adult?
Are formal qualifications more useful than learning by doing?
How has online learning changed how people acquire skills?

cards.prompt: Describe a journey that did not go as planned.
bullets: And explain how the experience affected you
part3Questions: Why do people enjoy travelling even when things go wrong?
How has technology changed the way people travel?
Is it better to plan a holiday in detail or to be spontaneous?

cards.prompt: Describe a time when you had to speak in public.
part3Questions: Why do many people fear public speaking?
Should public-speaking skills be taught in schools?
How important is it for professionals to communicate well in public?

cards.prompt: Describe a celebration that is important in your country.
bullets: And explain why it is significant
part3Questions: Why do traditions remain important even in modern societies?
Are national celebrations becoming more commercial?
Should children learn about the cultural traditions of other countries?

cards.prompt: Describe an event you attended that you enjoyed.
bullets: And explain why you enjoyed it
part3Questions: Are live events more engaging than watching them online?
How do large public events affect a city's economy?
Should governments fund cultural events out of public money?

cards.prompt: Describe a time when you celebrated an achievement.
bullets: And explain why this achievement was important to you
part3Questions: Is it healthy to celebrate small achievements as well as big ones?
How can families help children take pride in their achievements?
Are individual achievements valued more than team achievements in your culture?

cards.prompt: Describe a hobby you would like to take up.
bullets: How you first heard about it
And explain what you would need to start
part3Questions: Why is it important for people to have hobbies?
Do hobbies bring people together or push them apart?
How have hobbies changed in the last generation?

cards.prompt: Describe a sport or physical activity you enjoy.
bullets: And explain how it makes you feel
part3Questions: Why do many adults stop being physically active?
Should physical education be compulsory in schools?
How can governments encourage healthier lifestyles?

cards.prompt: Describe a skill you have that you are proud of.
bullets: How long it took to develop
And explain why you are proud of it
part3Questions: Are practical skills valued as much as academic skills today?
Should schools teach more life skills?
Why are some skills passed down through generations?

cards.prompt: Describe a meal you enjoyed cooking.
bullets: And explain why you enjoyed making it
part3Questions: Why are home-cooked meals becoming less common in many countries?
How is food connected to identity and culture?
What can governments do to promote healthier eating?

cards.prompt: Describe a film or series that you would recommend.
bullets: And explain why you recommend it
part3Questions: Why have streaming platforms changed how people watch films?
Do films from your country accurately represent local life?
Should governments support their own film industries?

cards.prompt: Describe a podcast or radio programme you like.
bullets: How often you listen to it
And explain why you find it interesting
part3Questions: Why has audio content become so popular again?
Is podcasting a reliable source of information?
How do podcasts compare with traditional news media?

cards.prompt: Describe a piece of news that caught your attention recently.
bullets: Where you heard or read it
And explain why it caught your attention
part3Questions: Has social media made news consumption better or worse?
How can people tell reliable news sources from unreliable ones?
Should governments regulate news media more strictly?

cards.prompt: Describe a website or app you use often.
bullets: How long you have used it
And explain how it has been useful to you
part3Questions: Are people becoming too dependent on apps for everyday tasks?
How can users protect their privacy online?
Should children's access to social media be restricted by law?

cards.prompt: Describe a time when you felt proud of someone close to you.
bullets: And explain why you felt proud
part3Questions: How do family members influence each other's achievements?
Is it healthy for parents to be very ambitious for their children?
Should success be measured in financial or personal terms?

cards.prompt: Describe a natural place you have visited.
bullets: And explain how the visit made you feel
part3Questions: Are people in your country becoming more or less interested in nature?
How can governments balance tourism with conservation?
Should children spend more time in natural environments?
